title: Google Maps in AI Studio: what the no-credit-card sandbox covers, and what changes when you go to production
summary: Google Maps Platform now works inside AI Studio with no credit card: 100 calls/day per API, reset every 24 hours. Here is what that covers and what production billing changes.

# Google Maps in AI Studio: what the no-credit-card sandbox covers, and what changes when you go to production


By OpenTools Team


·


November 11, 2026


Google announced on November 9, 2026 that Google Maps Platform can be used directly inside Google AI Studio. Developers can prompt Gemini for a map‑based app and get a live preview without a credit card. Google says the sandbox allows 100 calls per day, per API, resetting every 24 hours. Production use or higher capacity requires linking a paid Google Cloud billing account, at which point standard Maps Platform pricing applies, including recurring monthly free usage per Google. This article maps the four API families (Maps, Places, Routes, Environment) to example app tasks and sets out a prototype‑to‑production checklist. It also lists what Google's announcements do not say, such as what counts as a call and what production rates apply. We did not test the feature.


##


What Google announced


On November 9, 2026, Google said developers can build with Google Maps Platform directly inside Google AI Studio.[1](https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/technology/developers-tools/build-google-maps-platform-ai-studio/) The workflow in Google's developer post is to describe an app to Gemini and let AI Studio handle configuration and API key management. AI Studio then loads a live, interactive map in the preview area.[2](https://developers.googleblog.com/from-prompt-to-app-build-with-google-maps-in-ai-studio/)


There are two setup paths. A developer with no Google Cloud project can start without a credit card. A developer with an existing Google Cloud project can have AI Studio detect and link it.[1](https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/technology/developers-tools/build-google-maps-platform-ai-studio/) The key handling is described by Google as secure. We have not independently audited it.


##


What the free sandbox covers


Google's wording is specific: "Daily quotas (100 calls/day, per API) reset every 24 hours and no credit card is required".[2](https://developers.googleblog.com/from-prompt-to-app-build-with-google-maps-in-ai-studio/) The footnote on both announcements says to try for free up to the daily quota limits.[1](https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/technology/developers-tools/build-google-maps-platform-ai-studio/)


The figure is 100 calls per day for each API. It is not described as 100 calls per app, per user or per account. The announcements do not say how a "call" is counted for each API, or exactly how a quota is scoped across projects. Google points readers to the Google Maps Platform documentation for quotas and supported APIs.[2](https://developers.googleblog.com/from-prompt-to-app-build-with-google-maps-in-ai-studio/) Google presents the quotas as protection against unexpected charges while experimenting. They are a prototyping allowance, not a production service guarantee.


##


Which API family maps to which task


Google lists four families as available in this integration, with example uses:[2](https://developers.googleblog.com/from-prompt-to-app-build-with-google-maps-in-ai-studio/)


- **Maps:** custom-styled map interfaces, photorealistic 3D cityscapes, data overlays.
- **Places:** conversational local search, place profiles, photo galleries, recommendations.
- **Routes:** multi-stop road-trip itineraries, commute calculators, transit-aware day planners.
- **Environment:** clean-air route finders, live pollen alerts, hyper-local environmental monitors.


Google also names three gallery examples you can remix. City Immersive Tour shows 3D city maps with custom flyover camera paths and place markers. Pet Grooming Route Optimizer uses the Routes API for multi-stop routes with fixed appointment times, priority stops and driver shift limits. Store Locator & Near Me Finder uses vector maps and the Places API for searches by distance, opening hours and branch details.


Because the quota is stated per API, an app that touches several families draws on each one's allowance separately. A store locator that loads a map and runs place searches uses the Maps and Places allowances. A route planner would use Routes. Google does not say how many calls a single user action triggers, so a prototype with a few testers could reach 100 calls in one API faster than expected. Whether a given gallery example works for your own use or deployment is something to check yourself. We did not test any of them.


##


Prototype-to-production checklist


Google's stated path to production is to link a Google Cloud billing account. That unlocks production-grade quotas and connects the app to standard Maps Platform pricing, which Google says includes recurring monthly free usage.[2](https://developers.googleblog.com/from-prompt-to-app-build-with-google-maps-in-ai-studio/) Both announcements say a paid Cloud billing account is required for production.[1](https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/technology/developers-tools/build-google-maps-platform-ai-studio/) A practical sequence based on those statements:


1. **List the API families your app needs** (Maps, Places, Routes, Environment) and note that the sandbox allowance applies to each separately.
2. **Test with the daily quota in mind.** If a feature fails after repeated use, a quota reached before the 24-hour reset is one possible cause. Check the Maps Platform quota documentation for how each API counts calls.
3. **Decide whether you are staying a prototype.** Google frames the no-card sandbox for experimenting. If you plan to launch, or need more than the daily limits, link a paid billing account.
4. **Link an existing Cloud project or set up billing before launch.** AI Studio can auto-connect an existing project, per Google.
5. **Check current pricing for each API you use.** Google says standard pricing applies with recurring monthly free usage, but the announcements give no rates or free-usage amounts. Use the pricing page for the APIs you chose.
6. **Review the app itself before deploying.** A prompt-generated preview shows the map loading. It does not show that the app handles errors, key restrictions, usage spikes or your own requirements.


##


Known and unknown


Confirmed by Google's announcements: Maps, Places, Routes and Environment APIs are available in AI Studio now. Setup requires no credit card for the sandbox. The quota is 100 calls per day per API, reset every 24 hours. Production needs a paid Cloud billing account.


Not stated in the sources: what counts as one call for each API, how the quotas are scoped across projects or users, which API versions or products are covered beyond the four families, and what production costs will be. These are Google's claims from its own announcements. We did not run the feature, so there is no independent evidence about setup time, preview behavior or key security.
